require 'grpc'
require 'concurrent'
require 'digest'
require 'jwt'

module AuthService
  # JWT signing configuration. In production, load these from a secure secret
  # store / KMS rather than hard-coding. HS256 secret shown for illustration;
  # prefer RS256/ES256 with a rotating public key set in real deployments.
  JWT_SECRET = ENV.fetch('JWT_SECRET')
  JWT_ALGORITHM = 'HS256'.freeze

  class TokenCache
    def initialize(max_size: 10000, ttl: 300)
      @store = Concurrent::Map.new
      @ttl = ttl
      @max_size = max_size
      @eviction_lock = Mutex.new
      @shutdown_in_progress = Concurrent::AtomicBoolean.new(false)
    end

    def lookup(cache_key)
      return nil if @shutdown_in_progress.true?
      entry = @store[cache_key]
      return nil unless entry
      if entry[:expires_at] < Time.now.to_f
        @store.delete(cache_key)
        return nil
      end
      entry[:value]
    end

    def store(cache_key, value, ttl_override: nil)
      return if @shutdown_in_progress.true?
      evict_if_full
      effective_ttl = ttl_override || @ttl
      @store[cache_key] = {
        value: value,
        expires_at: Time.now.to_f + effective_ttl,
        stored_at: Time.now.to_f
      }
    end

    def invalidate(cache_key)
      @store.delete(cache_key)
    end

    def begin_shutdown
      @shutdown_in_progress.make_true
    end

    def shutdown_in_progress?
      @shutdown_in_progress.true?
    end

    def freeze_cache
      # During graceful shutdown, we do NOT extend TTLs.
      # Instead we disable cache reads/writes to force
      # fresh auth checks for any remaining requests.
      @shutdown_in_progress.make_true
    end

    private

    def evict_if_full
      return unless @store.size >= @max_size
      @eviction_lock.synchronize do
        return unless @store.size >= @max_size
        now = Time.now.to_f
        @store.each_pair do |key, entry|
          @store.delete(key) if entry[:expires_at] < now
        end
      end
    end
  end

  class AuthorizationInterceptor < GRPC::ServerInterceptor
    def initialize(cache)
      @cache = cache
      @permission_db = PermissionDatabase.new
    end

    def request_response(request:, call:, method:)
      token = extract_token(call)
      return yield if token.nil?

      # Verify the JWT signature and claims BEFORE trusting any of its
      # contents. A token that fails verification is rejected outright and
      # is never used to build a cache key or drive authorization.
      claims = verify_token(token)
      raise GRPC::Unauthenticated.new('Invalid token') if claims.nil?

      cache_key = compute_cache_key(claims, method)
      cached_result = @cache.lookup(cache_key)

      if cached_result
        apply_authorization(call, cached_result)
      else
        auth_result = @permission_db.check_permissions(claims, method)
        cache_ttl = determine_ttl(auth_result)
        @cache.store(cache_key, auth_result, ttl_override: cache_ttl)
        apply_authorization(call, auth_result)
      end

      yield
    end

    private

    def compute_cache_key(claims, method)
      # Cache key includes verified token identity and target method.
      token_id = claims['sub'] || 'anonymous'
      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest("#{token_id}:#{method}")
    end

    def determine_ttl(auth_result)
      # Denied results get shorter TTL to allow quick recovery
      # after permission grants
      auth_result[:permitted] ? 300 : 30
    end

    def extract_token(call)
      metadata = call.metadata
      metadata['authorization']&.sub(/^Bearer /, '')
    end

    # Verifies the JWT signature, algorithm and expiry. Returns the decoded
    # claims hash on success, or nil if the token is invalid. This closes the
    # forged-token / cache-poisoning hole where the payload was previously
    # decoded and trusted without any signature check.
    def verify_token(token)
      payload, _header = JWT.decode(
        token,
        JWT_SECRET,
        true,
        {
          algorithm: JWT_ALGORITHM,
          verify_expiration: true
        }
      )
      payload
    rescue JWT::DecodeError, JWT::ExpiredSignature, JWT::VerificationError
      nil
    end

    def apply_authorization(call, auth_result)
      unless auth_result[:permitted]
        raise GRPC::PermissionDenied.new('Access denied')
      end
    end
  end

  class GracefulShutdownHandler
    def initialize(server, cache)
      @server = server
      @cache = cache
      @drain_timeout = 30
    end

    def initiate_shutdown
      @cache.begin_shutdown
      # Freeze cache to prevent serving stale auth decisions
      # during connection drain period
      @cache.freeze_cache

      # Begin draining connections
      drain_thread = Thread.new do
        sleep @drain_timeout
        @server.stop
      end

      @server.stop
      drain_thread.join
    end
  end

  class PermissionDatabase
    def check_permissions(claims, method)
      # Simulated permission check against backing store using verified claims
      { permitted: validate_token_permissions(claims, method),
        roles: extract_roles(claims),
        checked_at: Time.now.to_f }
    end

    private

    def validate_token_permissions(claims, method)
      # Real implementation would check verified claims against DB
      true
    end

    def extract_roles(claims)
      Array(claims['roles']).any? ? Array(claims['roles']) : ['user']
    end
  end

  def self.run_server
    cache = TokenCache.new(max_size: 10000, ttl: 300)
    interceptors = [AuthorizationInterceptor.new(cache)]

    server = GRPC::RpcServer.new(interceptors: interceptors)

    # Use TLS credentials so bearer tokens and auth decisions are never sent
    # in cleartext. Certificate/key paths come from the environment.
    cert_chain = File.read(ENV.fetch('GRPC_TLS_CERT'))
    private_key = File.read(ENV.fetch('GRPC_TLS_KEY'))
    root_certs = ENV['GRPC_TLS_CA'] ? File.read(ENV['GRPC_TLS_CA']) : nil
    credentials = GRPC::Core::ServerCredentials.new(
      root_certs,
      [{ private_key: private_key, cert_chain: cert_chain }],
      false
    )
    server.add_http2_port('0.0.0.0:50051', credentials)

    shutdown_handler = GracefulShutdownHandler.new(server, cache)

    Signal.trap('TERM') { shutdown_handler.initiate_shutdown }
    Signal.trap('INT') { shutdown_handler.initiate_shutdown }

    server.run_till_terminated
  end
end
